figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Per-prediction reliability of encoder$+$ST models decays smoothly with gene-space distance to the training perturbations. (A) Encoder coupled with ST decoder for perturbation prediction. An upstream encoder (any single-cell foundation model or cell embedding, e.g., SE-600M, Tahoe-x1, scGPT) embeds each control cell, and the perturbation embedding is added to every cell embedding ($\oplus$). The ST decoder ($8$ attention blocks) and a gene decoder map these to predicted cells. Predictions are averaged into a pseudobulk for evaluation (§3). Each cell is drawn as a vector. Before $L_{0}$ (black outline) the cell vectors point in different directions, and after it they point along one shared direction with different lengths. This is the low-rank output of the $L_{0}$ self-attention (§4.2). (B) HepG2. Each gray dot is one of the $945$ held-out perturbations under Tahoe-x1$+$ST, plotted as Pearson delta correlation (PDC, Eq. (1)) against the cosine distance in gene space from its response to the nearest training response. Lines are kernel-smoothed trends per encoder (Spearman $\rho$ in the legend). RPL6 (small distance) is predicted reliably and SNAPC5 (large distance) is not. The pattern replicates across all four cell lines (§B.2). The deployable analog (Definition 1) and the calibrated threshold are developed in §4.3.
figures.headline: Under Tahoe-x1 plus ST on HepG2, accuracy falls smoothly as held-out responses move farther from training responses.
citing_sentences: STATE [2] pairs a cell-state encoder with a trainable state-transition (ST) decoder: the encoder represents control cells, and the decoder combines these representations with a perturbation embedding to predict post-perturbation gene expression (Figure 1A).
PDC declines smoothly as the cosine distance from an observed response to its nearest training response increases (Figure 1B).
We study predictors that couple an upstream encoder with a state-transition (ST) decoder, henceforth encoder$+$ST (Figure 1A).

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: How the decoder reads the perturbation. (A) PDC after replacing the output of one attention layer with a single random direction, relative to the decoder without the intervention (mean over the four cell lines; band, range). (B) Per-perturbation PDC with and without an intervention on the top $L_{0}$ component, which keeps its direction and sets its size to the mean over perturbations (left), or keeps its size and takes the direction of another perturbation (right). Numbers give the mean change. (C) PDC after projecting the $L_{0}$ output onto $k$ directions shared by all perturbations and estimated from training activations, or onto $k$ random directions, relative to the decoder without the intervention. For scGPT$+$ST one direction is too few even for each perturbation’s own top direction (Table 1). The perturbation enters at $L_{0}$ as a direction in a small shared subspace, and the perturbation-specific signal lies in this direction.
figures.headline: A random direction at the first attention layer removes accuracy, while the same replacement at later layers leaves it near unchanged.
citing_sentences: Replacing the layer’s output with a random direction removes the PDC of SE$+$ST and more than half of the PDC of Tahoe$+$ST, while the same replacement at any of $L_{1}$ to $L_{7}$ leaves PDC close to that of the decoder without the intervention (Figure 2A).

Setting the size of the top component to its mean over perturbations leaves PDC unchanged for SE$+$ST and Tahoe$+$ST, while giving each perturbation the direction of another perturbation lowers it (Figure 2B).

A single basis estimated from training activations and shared by all perturbations preserves PDC with at most $32$ of the $328$ dimensions, while the same number of random directions does not (Figure 2C).

(B) Mean PDC of the accepted and rejected predictions under the pooled threshold $\tau\approx 0.10$ in each encoder–cell configuration; numbers give the share accepted. The score selects predictions nearly as well as the oracle, and one threshold selects accurate predictions in every configuration.

abstract: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction’s reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder’s first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto $4$–$32$ fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder’s reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation’s observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of $0.81$ with PDC, close to the $0.88$ obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

sections.body: The paper asks why simple linear baselines match foundation-model perturbation predictors and how a user can tell whether one prediction is reliable. It studies three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, Tahoe-x1) coupled to the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE, across four CRISPRi cell lines. Two held-out HepG2 examples show the contrast. RPL6 is predicted accurately because knockdowns of other ribosomal genes in training produce similar responses. SNAPC5 lies far from all training responses and is predicted poorly. The authors list three contributions: a low-rank bottleneck in the decoder, an explanation for why baselines match the models, and predicted-NN-distance, a per-prediction confidence score.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Perturbation predictions lose accuracy as their responses move away from training responses, so each prediction needs a reliability score.

sections.body: This section places the work among perturbation predictors, from latent-arithmetic VAEs and optimal transport to recent single-cell foundation models and concurrent diffusion and ranking models. It notes that linear baselines match these models on standard splits, and that a predictor can score well by capturing response patterns shared across perturbations. The authors apply activation patching and low-rank projections from mechanistic interpretability to the ST decoder. For deployment they use Learn-then-Test, a conformal prediction method, to select a threshold on the confidence score with a finite-sample guarantee. Extended related work is in Appendix H.
sections.heading: Related work
sections.headline: Recent encoder-decoder predictors match linear baselines, and the authors open the decoder's first attention layer to find why.

sections.body: Each predictor pairs a frozen encoder with an ST decoder of eight attention blocks. The data are the Replogle–Nadig CRISPRi panel in HepG2, Jurkat, RPE1 and K562 under the STATE few-shot protocol, giving twelve encoder–cell configurations. Accuracy is per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC), the correlation across genes between predicted and observed change relative to control. The audit has three steps. A ridge or MLP probe reads the decoder inputs. The first-layer attention output is truncated to its top k singular components, with k set to 1, 4, 8, 16 or 32. The leading direction is then swapped between encoders. Predicted-NN-distance is the cosine distance from the predicted response to its nearest training response. A prediction is accepted when this score is at most a threshold.
sections.heading: Methods
sections.headline: The methods project the first attention output onto top singular or fixed training directions and score each prediction by predicted-NN-distance.

sections.body: The section compares the three encoder-plus-ST predictors with a ridge regression, CPA and the train-mean response. Over all held-out perturbations, each decoder and its ridge baseline fall within 0.04 PDC of each other. On perturbations far from training (cosine distance above 0.5), full decoder PDC is 0.071–0.140, close to the train-mean value of 0.073. Keeping only the top first-layer component changes mean PDC by at most 0.003 for SE+ST and Tahoe+ST. Replacing the first-layer output with a random direction removes the accuracy of SE+ST, while the same change at later layers leaves PDC close to the unintervened value. A single basis fixed from training activations preserves PDC with at most 32 of 328 dimensions. An oracle that averages the nearest training responses scores 0.137 PDC above the decoder on average.
sections.heading: Results
sections.headline: Decoder accuracy falls far from training, and its first attention layer passes perturbation signal through a few fixed directions.

sections.body: The discussion argues that these predictors are reliable when a held-out response resembles a training response, so benchmark scores depend largely on how many test perturbations lie close to training. It suggests that the first-layer direction test could be run on other perturbation decoders. Predicted-NN-distance needs only the prediction and the training responses, so it can be computed before an experiment. The broader impacts note a risk that accepted predictions are treated as measured responses, although some are wrong. Limitations include one decoder architecture, three encoders, four CRISPRi cell lines and Tahoe-100M drug data. The bottleneck is clearest for SE+ST. The score is weaker when a whole gene family is absent from training, and the Learn-then-Test guarantee fails when deployment perturbations lie farther from training than the calibration perturbations.
sections.heading: Discussion
sections.headline: Benchmark scores mostly reflect how many test perturbations lie near training, and a threshold on the score transfers to held-out cell lines.

sections.body: This section names two NIH awards, U24DK138515 and OT2OD038003, as support for all authors. It states that the authors declare no competing interests. It contains no methods, results or claims about the perturbation predictors. The text gives no further funders or disclosures beyond these two awards and the statement.

sections.body: The appendix gives the audit configurations and hyperparameters (Table 2) and the probe settings (Table 3). It covers the cell-line splits, the hidden-state rank diagnostics, and the swaps of first-layer directions between encoders and between cell lines. Further sections report per-cell-line baseline comparisons, gene-family analyses of the leading direction, the confidence-score threshold procedures, drug-perturbation results on Tahoe-100M, and extended related work. The compute statement reports about 780 GPU-hours for all batch jobs, including runs not reported in the paper. The last section describes the use of LLM-based assistants for code and writing, and the authors take full responsibility for the content.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists configurations and hyperparameters, probe settings, intervention and threshold details, per-cell-line results, gene-family analyses, and related work.
